    def skin_depth(omega: float, sigma_earth: float) -> float:
    """Electromagnetic skin depth in soil.

    Returns $\\delta = \\sqrt{2 / (\\omega \\mu_0 \\sigma)}$ in
    metres. Diverges at $\\omega = 0$ (purely conductive earth-
    return path); the caller must handle that case by skipping the
    Carson correction altogether.

    Parameters
    ----------
    omega
        Angular frequency $\\omega = 2\\pi f$ in rad/s.
    sigma_earth
        Earth conductivity $\\sigma$ in S/m.

    Returns
    -------
    delta : float
        Skin depth in metres. ``+inf`` when ``omega`` or
        ``sigma_earth`` is zero.
    """
    if omega <= 0.0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0:
        return math.inf
    return math.sqrt(2.0 / (omega * MU_0 * sigma_earth))

    Sommerfeld / Pollaczek earth return (ADR-0006)¶

    sommerfeld_inductance ¶

    Geometric Sommerfeld earth-return Green function (ADR-0006).

    This module implements the rigorous geometric formulation of the inductive earth-return coupling described in ADR-0006. Compared to ADR-0005's Carson per-meter scaling, it integrates the actual vector-potential Green's function over the segment-pair geometry, which correctly handles short wires, non-parallel arrangements, and layered earth.

    Mathematical background

    For a horizontal current element in a stratified, quasi-static medium (\(z > 0\) soil, \(z < 0\) air, layer \(k\) with \(\gamma_k^2 = j\omega\mu_0\sigma_k\) and vertical wavenumber \(u_k = \sqrt{\lambda^2 + \gamma_k^2}\), \(u_0 = \lambda\) in air; time convention \(e^{+j\omega t}\)), the vector-potential Green's function of a source at depth \(z'\) and an observer at depth \(z\) is

    \[ G(\rho, z, z') \;=\; \delta_{kj}\,\frac{e^{-\gamma_k R}}{R} \;+\; \int_0^{\infty}\! \lambda\,F_{kj}(\lambda; z, z')\, J_0(\lambda\rho)\,d\lambda , \]

    with \(k\) / \(j\) the layers of observer / source. The spectral amplitude \(F\) follows from the continuity of \(A\) and \(\partial A/\partial z\) at every interface. For source and observer in the same layer \(k\) (top at \(z_{k-1}\), thickness \(t\), depths \(h, h'\) measured from its top) it is the closed form

    \[ F_{kk} \;=\; \frac{\tilde R_\uparrow e^{-u_k(h+h')} + \tilde R_\downarrow e^{-u_k(2t-h-h')} + \tilde R_\uparrow\tilde R_\downarrow\bigl[e^{-u_k(2t-(h-h'))} + e^{-u_k(2t+(h-h'))}\bigr]} {u_k\,\bigl(1 - \tilde R_\uparrow \tilde R_\downarrow e^{-2u_k t}\bigr)}, \]

    where \(\tilde R_\uparrow\), \(\tilde R_\downarrow\) are the generalised reflection coefficients of the stack above and below layer \(k\) (bottom-up / top-down recursions over \(r_{k,m} = (u_k - u_m)/(u_k + u_m)\)). For the homogeneous half-space this is the familiar \((\lambda/u_1)\Gamma e^{-u_1(h+h')}\) with \(\Gamma = (u_1-\lambda)/(u_1+\lambda)\); for two layers it is the four-term buried-in-layer-1 amplitude validated against Tsiamitros (2005) Eq. (8) (WP-D2, 2026-07-20); for \(n \ge 3\) layers the generalised \(\tilde R_\downarrow\) makes it exact as well (review pass 10, finding 10.35 — the historic \(n \ge 3\) path used the single air-image form and was 17–25 % off in \(X'\)). Pairs in different layers (including a buried / overhead pair over a layered earth) use the transmitted amplitude, obtained from the same interface conditions by a small linear solve per \(\lambda\).

    The overhead pair keeps Carson's geometry, \(\lambda F_{00} = -\Gamma_s(\lambda) e^{-\lambda(H+H')}\), with the surface reflection coefficient \(\Gamma_s\) of the whole stack.

    Earth-return correction and image conventions

    The functions here return the earth-return correction \(\Delta Z\) that is added to \(j\omega L\), the Neumann partial-inductance matrix of groundfield.coupling.inductance.build_inductance_matrix(). The correction depends on which image that matrix carries (image=):

    • "none" — \(\Delta G = G - 1/R\), the exact quasi-static correction to free space. At DC the soil is magnetically transparent: no image at all.
    • "additive" (historic default, ADR-0004) — the matrix carries the perfect-magnetic-mirror image \(L_\text{img}\); the correction removes it exactly: \(\Delta Z_\text{additive} = \Delta Z_\text{none} - j\omega L_\text{img}\), with \(L_\text{img}\) computed by the same routine that added it (closed form for parallel pairs, the mirrored orientation for inclined and vertical segments).
    • "antiparallel" — \(\Delta Z_\text{none} + j\omega L_\text{img}\); for a pair on opposite sides of the surface, whose anti-parallel baseline is zero (a perfect conductor screens the soil), \(\Delta Z_\text{none} + j\omega L_\text{dir}\).

    Before review pass 10 the image was removed as \(-1/R'\) integrated by the 16x16 outer rule and weighted with the direct orientation: vertical segments kept twice the image in the \(\sigma \to 0\) limit, and segments much longer than twice their depth lost 0.6 % (25 m) to 5.7 % (50 m) of the image term (finding 10.46).

    Numerical method

    Each segment pair is integrated by 16x16 Gauss–Legendre over the two segments; the closed-form direct term \((e^{-\gamma R}-1)/R\) is evaluated at every node, the spectral part \(S(\rho) = \int \lambda F J_0(\lambda\rho)\,d\lambda\) on 24 log-spaced \(\rho\) nodes and interpolated (segments assumed approximately horizontal, mean depths per segment). Segments that cross the soil surface or a layer interface are split there first.

    Along the line of closest approach of a segment with itself, or of two segments that come close (wires beside each other, a core in its shield), the integrand has a kink: the \(\gamma^2 R/2\) term of the direct part and the corresponding term of \(S\), smoothed only over the decay length of the spectral weight. The tensor rule cannot follow it: the self correction of a buried segment was 4.8e-4 off at a quarter skin depth (100 Ω·m), up to 1.5e-3 for two wires 1 mm apart in 30 over 1000 Ω·m. Since user decision Q34

    • the self term of a (sub-)segment is the exact one-dimensional reduction \(2\int_0^L (L - u)\,g(u)\,du\) of its double integral (one spectral plan per segment, so \(g\) depends on \(u = |s - s'|\) only), with graded 16-node panels (_self_values());
    • a close pair (closest distance of the Gauss nodes below half the longer segment) gets a graded rule along the line of closest approach (_close_pair_values()); for two coinciding segments it is the self rule;
    • the other pairs keep the tensor rule (16x16, composite for segments longer than a quarter skin depth).

    The self correction is within 1.1e-9 of a refined rule (1024 logarithmic \(\lambda\) nodes) and of an independent reference (closed-form direct part, the \(\mathrm{Ji}_0\) kernel of the spectral part; audit W3B) from 1 m and 0.01 skin depths to 3 km at 50 Hz and 1 kHz and has no step where the rule changes (below 3e-13); close pairs are within about 4e-8 of the same two references (3.5e-8 for two 1 m wires 1 mm apart in 30 over 1000 Ω·m at 1 kHz, 2.7e-9 at a quarter skin depth). Up to audit W3B-01 the logarithmic region of the \(\lambda\) grid had 64 nodes and short segments missed the skin-scale part of \(S\): 1e-5 … 7.4e-5 at 0.01 skin depths, up to 3e-4 at 1 m (9e-9 of the input impedance of a 200 m PEN in 1 m pieces). Both rules cost at most linearly in the length: a lumped conductor of 2 km between a rod and a junction is solved in 1.1 s within 0.21 GB (audit W2B-05: 28 s, 1.6 GB, about \(L^{2.7}\)).

    The \(\lambda\) quadrature (review pass 10, finding 10.36) follows the F14 policy of groundfield.coupling.layered_green: a logarithmic region on \([\epsilon, \lambda_\text{b}]\) with \(\lambda_\text{b} \le \pi/(4\rho_\text{max})\) so that it is free of \(J_0\) oscillations, followed by Gauss panels of width \(\le \pi/\rho_\text{max}\) (16 nodes per \(J_0\) period), geometrically graded near the skin and decay scales, up to \(\lambda_\text{max} = 30/z\). Before the fix the log region ended at \(\max(p_\text{skin}, 1/z)\) regardless of the distance, so \(J_0\) went unresolved for distant pairs (Re −24 % at 200 m, +274 % at 400 m), and a 4096-panel cap truncated silently. The node budget is now explicit: beyond a soft limit the density drops to 8 nodes per period, and a SommerfeldResolutionWarning is raised instead of a silent truncation when even that does not fit.

    build_sommerfeld_correction_matrices() evaluates several frequencies at once (finding 10.60): geometry, \(\lambda\) grid and the Bessel table are built once per pair and reused for every frequency whose grid is identical (the common case — the grid depends on the frequency only through skin scales above \(1/z\)). Each frequency's matrix equals the single-frequency result bit for bit.

    Limit checks (built into the test suite)
    • \(\sigma_e\to 0\): \(\Delta Z_\text{none} \to 0\), and with image="additive" the correction cancels the mirror exactly for every orientation.
    • \(\sigma_e\to\infty\), overhead pair: \(-\Gamma \to -1\), the net image becomes the anti-parallel PEC image (Carson's baseline).
    • \(\sigma_e\to\infty\), buried pair: \(e^{-\gamma R} \to 0\) — the conductor is screened by the surrounding medium.
    • Long parallel buried wires: the per-metre limit reproduces Pollaczek's \(\frac{j\omega\mu_0}{2\pi}\bigl[K_0(\gamma d) - K_0(\gamma D') + J_P\bigr]\).
    • A three-layer earth with \(\rho_2 = \rho_3\) reproduces the two-layer result.
    References
    • Stratton, J. A. (1941). Electromagnetic Theory, McGraw-Hill, §9-10 — derivation of the half-space vector potential.
    • Sommerfeld, A. (1909). Über die Ausbreitung der Wellen in der drahtlosen Telegraphie. Ann. Phys. 28(4), 665–736.
    • Wait, J. R. (1972). Electromagnetic Waves in Stratified Media, Pergamon. Ch. 3.
    • Chew, W. C. (1995). Waves and Fields in Inhomogeneous Media, IEEE Press, §2.1 (generalised reflection coefficients).
    • Tsiamitros, D. A. et al. (2005). Earth return path impedances of underground cables for the two-layer earth case. IEEE Trans. Power Delivery 20(3), 2174–2181.

Future hardware-accelerated backends (e.g. an MLX path on Apple silicon) must honour the same precision. np.complex128 is the default at every entry point and is preserved through the Sommerfeld quadrature; do not silently down-cast to FP32 in a derived backend.

    def layer_of(self, depth: float) -> int:
    """Layer index (1-based) that contains ``depth`` (m, > 0 in soil).

    A point exactly on an interface belongs to the lower layer.
    """
    return 1 + bisect.bisect_right(self.interface_depths, float(depth))

    SommerfeldResolutionWarning ¶

    Bases: UserWarning

    The Sommerfeld quadrature could not resolve the \(J_0\) oscillations.

    The linear region of the Hankel grid places one Gauss panel per \(J_0(\lambda s)\) period, so the node count grows like \(\lambda_\text{max}\,s\). A hard node budget (_HANKEL_MAX_LINEAR_NODES) bounds the transient allocation; when that budget forces fewer than _HANKEL_MIN_NODES_PER_OSCILLATION nodes per period the quadrature is no longer converged and this warning is raised instead of returning a silently wrong number (a coarse grid on an oscillatory integrand does not merely lose digits — it can flip the sign of the result).

    The remedy is always to lower lambda_max_factor or to reduce the horizontal distance range of the group. Lowering the factor does not lose accuracy: the truncated tail is subtracted in closed form (_reflected_image_terms()), so a smaller \(\lambda_\text{max}\) only moves work from the quadrature into the exact image sum. Silence with warnings.simplefilter("ignore", SommerfeldResolutionWarning) only if the affected entries are known to be negligible.

    def build_sommerfeld_correction_matrices(
    seg_endpoints: np.ndarray,  # shape (M, 2, 3)
    wire_radii: np.ndarray | None = None,
    *,
    omegas: Sequence[float],
    earth: LayeredEarth,
    image: ImageConvention = "additive",
    method: SommerfeldAssembly = "exact",
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sommerfeld earth-return correction matrices for several frequencies.

    Multi-frequency form of :func:`build_sommerfeld_correction_matrix`
    (finding 10.60): per segment pair the outer geometry, the
    $\\lambda$ grid and the Bessel table $J_0(\\lambda\\rho)$ — about
    three quarters of the historic per-frequency cost — are built once
    and reused for every frequency with the same grid. Entry ``k``
    equals ``build_sommerfeld_correction_matrix(..., omega=omegas[k])``
    bit for bit.

    Parameters
    ----------
    seg_endpoints
        Array of shape ``(M, 2, 3)``: start and end point (m) of every
        inductive branch segment.
    wire_radii
        Per-branch wire radii in m. Only used with an image convention:
        a mirrored partner that interpenetrates a segment is evaluated as
        a touching wire, as in
        :func:`~groundfield.coupling.inductance.build_inductance_matrix`
        (pass the same radii for an exact match in that degenerate case).
    omegas
        Angular frequencies in rad/s; entries ``<= 0`` give zeros.
    earth
        Layered-earth configuration.
    image
        Image convention of the inductance matrix the corrections are
        added to: ``"additive"`` (default), ``"none"`` (exact baseline,
        cheapest; what the solver assembles) or ``"antiparallel"``.
    method
        ``"exact"`` (default): every segment pair gets its own
        $\\lambda$ grid and Bessel table, and $S(\\rho)$ is interpolated
        linearly on 24 nodes per pair. ``"tabulated"`` (finding 10.60;
        what the solver uses by default since 2026.11,
        :attr:`groundfield.Engine.sommerfeld_assembly`): sub-segments are grouped by depth, every pair of depth
        groups shares one table of $S(\\rho)$ per frequency (cubic
        spline in $\\ln(\\rho + z)$ on the $\\lambda$ grid of the
        group's largest distance), and the outer nodes of all pairs are
        evaluated vectorised; blocks of fewer than 64 sub-segment pairs
        use the exact rule. In both assemblies the self term of every
        segment and every close pair get the rules of user decision Q34
        (one-dimensional self rule, graded close-pair rule; see the module
        docstring), which also bound the cost of long conductors.

    Returns
    -------
    dZ : np.ndarray, shape (n_f, M, M), dtype complex
        Symmetric correction matrices in Ω.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``image`` is not one of ``"none"``, ``"additive"``,
        ``"antiparallel"``, or ``method`` is not ``"exact"`` or
        ``"tabulated"``.
    """
    mode = _resolve_image(image, None)
    if method not in _ASSEMBLIES:
        raise ValueError(f"method must be one of {_ASSEMBLIES}, got {method!r}")
    omegas = [float(om) for om in np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(omegas, dtype=float))]
    seg_endpoints = np.asarray(seg_endpoints, dtype=float)
    M = seg_endpoints.shape[0]
    out = np.zeros((len(omegas), M, M), dtype=complex)
    if M == 0 or all(om <= 0.0 for om in omegas):
        return out
    L_img = None
    if mode != "none":
        # The image block of build_inductance_matrix(image=mode); with
        # "antiparallel" a pair on opposite sides of the surface has no
        # baseline, so its correction moves by the direct mutual instead
        # (audit A2C-1).
        L_img = _image_inductance_matrix(seg_endpoints, wire_radii=wire_radii)
        if mode == "antiparallel":
            opposite = _opposite_sides(seg_endpoints[:, 0], seg_endpoints[:, 1])
            if opposite.any():
                L_dir = _direct_mutual_matrix(seg_endpoints, wire_radii)
                L_img[opposite] = L_dir[opposite]
    if method == "tabulated":
        out = _tabulated_values_none(seg_endpoints, omegas, earth)
    else:
        for i in range(M):
            p1_i = seg_endpoints[i, 0]
            p2_i = seg_endpoints[i, 1]
            for j in range(i, M):
                sign = 1.0 if i == j else _same_segment(p1_i, p2_i, *seg_endpoints[j])
                if sign != 0.0:
                    vals = sign * _pair_values_none(
                        p1_i, p2_i, p1_i, p2_i, omegas, earth, same=True
                    )
                else:
                    vals = _pair_values_none(
                        p1_i,
                        p2_i,
                        seg_endpoints[j, 0],
                        seg_endpoints[j, 1],
                        omegas,
                        earth,
                    )
                out[:, i, j] = vals
                out[:, j, i] = vals
    if L_img is not None:
        sign = -1.0 if mode == "additive" else 1.0
        for k, om in enumerate(omegas):
            if om > 0.0:
                out[k] += sign * 1j * om * L_img
    return out

    def build_sommerfeld_correction_matrix(
    seg_endpoints: np.ndarray,  # shape (M, 2, 3)
    wire_radii: np.ndarray | None = None,
    *,
    omega: float,
    earth: LayeredEarth,
    image: ImageConvention = "additive",
    method: SommerfeldAssembly = "exact",
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Assemble the dense Sommerfeld earth-return correction matrix.

    The output is the σ-dependent addition to the Neumann inductance
    matrix of
    :func:`groundfield.coupling.inductance.build_inductance_matrix`
    built with the same image convention:

    .. code-block:: python

        Z_b = jω · L(image=image) + dZ_Sommerfeld(image=image)

    For ``earth.n_layers == 1`` this is the homogeneous-earth
    Pollaczek kernel; for ``n >= 2`` the exact layered kernel is used.
    Several frequencies at once: :func:`build_sommerfeld_correction_matrices`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    seg_endpoints
        Array of shape ``(M, 2, 3)`` with the start- and end-points
        (m) of every distributed-conductor longitudinal-branch segment.
    wire_radii
        Per-branch wire radii in m (only used with an image convention,
        see :func:`build_sommerfeld_correction_matrices`).
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.
    earth
        Layered-earth configuration.
    image
        ``"additive"`` (default), ``"none"`` or ``"antiparallel"`` —
        see the module docstring.
    method
        ``"exact"`` (default of this function) or ``"tabulated"`` (the
        solver's default, see :func:`build_sommerfeld_correction_matrices`).

    Returns
    -------
    dZ : np.ndarray, shape (M, M), dtype complex
        Symmetric Sommerfeld correction matrix in $\\Omega$.
    """
    if omega <= 0.0:
        return np.zeros(
            (np.asarray(seg_endpoints).shape[0],) * 2,
            dtype=complex,
        )
    return build_sommerfeld_correction_matrices(
        seg_endpoints,
        wire_radii,
        omegas=[omega],
        earth=earth,
        image=image,
        method=method,
    )[0]

    earth_return_correction_homogeneous(*, rho: float, z_i: float, z_j: float, omega: float, sigma_earth: float) -> complex

    σ-dependent earth-return correction beyond the additive mirror.

    Point-kernel form of the buried–buried Pollaczek correction (see the module docstring):

    \[ \Delta G \;=\; \frac{e^{-\gamma R} - 1}{R} \;-\; \frac{1}{R'} \;+\; \int_0^\infty \frac{\lambda}{u_1}\, \Gamma(\lambda)\, e^{-u_1 (z + z')}\, J_0(\lambda\rho)\,d\lambda, \]

    with \(R = \sqrt{\rho^2 + (z - z')^2}\), \(R' = \sqrt{\rho^2 + (z + z')^2}\). This is the σ-dependent piece to be added to the ADR-0004 result (which carries \(1/R + 1/R'\)): the \(-1/R'\) removes the additive mirror, the attenuated direct term carries the buried-path earth-return resistance, and the \(\lambda/u_1\)-weighted reflection is the genuine soil-side boundary response.

    Limit checks:

    • \(\sigma_e \to 0\): \(\gamma \to 0\), \(\Gamma \to 0\) — correction \(\to -1/R'\) → cancels the ADR-0004 image, total → free space \(1/R\).
    • \(\sigma_e \to \infty\): \(e^{-\gamma R} \to 0\), \(\lambda/u_1 \to 0\) — correction \(\to -1/R - 1/R'\), total → 0 (buried conductor screened by the surrounding medium).

    def earth_return_correction_homogeneous(
    *,
    rho: float,
    z_i: float,
    z_j: float,
    omega: float,
    sigma_earth: float,
) -> complex:
    """σ-dependent earth-return correction beyond the additive mirror.

    Point-kernel form of the **buried–buried** Pollaczek correction
    (see the module docstring):

    $$
    \\Delta G \\;=\\; \\frac{e^{-\\gamma R} - 1}{R}
    \\;-\\; \\frac{1}{R'}
    \\;+\\; \\int_0^\\infty \\frac{\\lambda}{u_1}\\,
    \\Gamma(\\lambda)\\, e^{-u_1 (z + z')}\\,
    J_0(\\lambda\\rho)\\,d\\lambda,
    $$

    with $R = \\sqrt{\\rho^2 + (z - z')^2}$,
    $R' = \\sqrt{\\rho^2 + (z + z')^2}$. This is the σ-dependent
    piece *to be added to the ADR-0004 result* (which carries
    $1/R + 1/R'$): the $-1/R'$ removes the additive mirror, the
    attenuated direct term carries the buried-path earth-return
    resistance, and the $\\lambda/u_1$-weighted reflection is the
    genuine soil-side boundary response.

    Limit checks:

    - $\\sigma_e \\to 0$: $\\gamma \\to 0$, $\\Gamma \\to 0$ —
      correction $\\to -1/R'$ → cancels the ADR-0004 image, total
      → free space $1/R$.
    - $\\sigma_e \\to \\infty$: $e^{-\\gamma R} \\to 0$,
      $\\lambda/u_1 \\to 0$ — correction $\\to -1/R - 1/R'$, total
      → 0 (buried conductor screened by the surrounding medium).

    Parameters
    ----------
    rho
        Horizontal distance between source and field point in m.
        Must be ≥ 0.
    z_i, z_j
        Depths (positive into soil) in m. Must be > 0 for the
        integral to converge.
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.
    sigma_earth
        Earth conductivity in S/m.

    Returns
    -------
    correction : complex
        The kernel above in 1/m (the pair integrals multiply by
        $j\\omega\\mu_0/(4\\pi)$ and integrate over both segments).
    """
    if omega <= 0.0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0:
        return 0.0 + 0.0j
    earth = LayeredEarth(rhos=(1.0 / sigma_earth,), thicknesses=())
    return earth_return_correction_layered(
        rho=rho, z_i=z_i, z_j=z_j, omega=omega, earth=earth
    )

    def earth_return_correction_layered(
    *,
    rho: float,
    z_i: float,
    z_j: float,
    omega: float,
    earth: LayeredEarth,
) -> complex:
    """Layered-earth analogue of :func:`earth_return_correction_homogeneous`.

    Buried–buried point kernel beyond the additive mirror,
    $\\Delta G = G - 1/R - 1/R'$, with the exact layered Green's
    function of the module docstring: the generalised-reflection
    closed form for points in the same layer, the transmitted amplitude
    otherwise. Review pass 10 (finding 10.46, pass-9 F50): the
    historic implementation used the single air-image form with the
    stack's surface reflection coefficient, whose reflected term has
    the **opposite sign** of the exact two-layer kernel (e.g.
    +8.7e-3 instead of −6.3e-3 at $\\rho = 0$ for earth (100, 10)
    Ω·m, $h_1$ = 3 m, 1 kHz, $z = z' = 0.6$ m).

    Parameters
    ----------
    rho
        Horizontal distance in m (≥ 0).
    z_i, z_j
        Depths of observer and source in m (> 0, in the soil).
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.
    earth
        Layered-earth configuration.

    Returns
    -------
    correction : complex
        Kernel value in 1/m.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``z_i`` or ``z_j`` is not positive (a point not buried) and
        ``omega`` is positive.
    """
    if omega <= 0.0:
        return 0.0 + 0.0j
    if z_i <= 0.0 or z_j <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"earth_return_correction_layered needs buried points (z > 0); "
            f"got z_i={z_i}, z_j={z_j}"
        )
    rho = float(rho)
    R_dir = math.sqrt(rho * rho + (z_i - z_j) ** 2)
    R_mir = math.sqrt(rho * rho + (z_i + z_j) ** 2)
    k_i = earth.layer_of(z_i)
    k_j = earth.layer_of(z_j)
    plan = _SpectralPlan.buried(earth, z_i, z_j, k_i, k_j)
    lambdas, weights = _build_lambda_grid(
        z_sum=plan.decay,
        rho_max=max(rho, 1e-6),
        omega=omega,
        sigma_top=1.0 / earth.rhos[plan.ref_layer - 1],
        scales=plan.scales(omega, earth),
    )
    spec = plan.weight(lambdas, omega, earth)
    reflected = complex(np.sum(weights * spec * j0(lambdas * rho)))
    if k_i == k_j:
        gamma = complex(np.sqrt(1j * omega * MU_0 / earth.rhos[k_i - 1]))
        if R_dir < 1e-9:
            direct = -gamma
        else:
            direct = (np.exp(-gamma * R_dir) - 1.0) / R_dir
    else:
        direct = 0.0
    return complex(direct) - 1.0 / max(R_mir, 1e-9) + reflected

    per_metre_mutual_impedance ¶

    per_metre_mutual_impedance(z_i: float, z_j: float, distance: float, *, omega: float, earth: LayeredEarth) -> complex

    Mutual impedance per metre of two infinite parallel horizontal wires.

    Exact quasi-static earth-return impedance (Ω/m) of two long parallel wires at depths z_i, z_j (m, z > 0 in the soil, z < 0 overhead; both on one side of the surface, buried ones in one layer) at the horizontal distance distance (m) over the layered earth: the line integral of the Green's function of the module docstring, \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} J_0(\lambda\sqrt{x^2 + s^2})\,ds = 2\cos(\lambda x)/\lambda\),

    \[ Z'(x) \;=\; \frac{j\omega\mu_0}{4\pi}\Bigl[2K_0(\gamma_k R) + \int_0^\infty w(\lambda)\,\frac{2\cos\lambda x}{\lambda}\,d\lambda\Bigr] \]

    for wires in layer \(k\) (\(R = \sqrt{x^2 + (z_i - z_j)^2}\), \(w\) the reflected amplitude of the same-layer kernel, exact for any number of layers), and \(\frac{j\omega\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_0^\infty [e^{-\lambda|z_i - z_j|} - \Gamma(\lambda)e^{-\lambda(h_i + h_j)}] \,2\cos(\lambda x)/\lambda\,d\lambda\) for overhead wires (Carson's integral with the surface reflection coefficient of the stack). The self impedance per metre of a wire is the value at distance equal to its radius (or GMR). The \(\lambda\) quadrature is the one of the segment pairs (finding 10.36) with four times the nodes. For a homogeneous earth this is Carson's (overhead) and Pollaczek's (buried) impedance; it agrees with Carson to 2e-9 and with the two-layer Pollaczek integral of groundfield.references.pollaczek to 5e-8 of the impedance (0.1 … 300 m). Against an independent integral (audit W3B-08: composite Gauss, checked against mpmath to 2e-15; one to four layers, 50 Hz and 1 kHz, 1 cm … 1 km) it is within 6e-8 of the earth-return correction up to 300 m and 7e-7 at 1 km for buried pairs, 4e-8 for overhead pairs; the remainder is not the logarithmic region of the \(\lambda\) grid (the same with 256 and 1024 nodes there).

    def per_metre_mutual_impedance(
    z_i: float,
    z_j: float,
    distance: float,
    *,
    omega: float,
    earth: LayeredEarth,
) -> complex:
    """Mutual impedance per metre of two infinite parallel horizontal wires.

    Exact quasi-static earth-return impedance (Ω/m) of two long parallel
    wires at depths ``z_i``, ``z_j`` (m, ``z > 0`` in the soil, ``z < 0``
    overhead; both on one side of the surface, buried ones in one layer) at
    the horizontal distance ``distance`` (m) over the layered earth: the
    line integral of the Green's function of the module docstring,
    $\\int_{-\\infty}^{\\infty} J_0(\\lambda\\sqrt{x^2 + s^2})\\,ds =
    2\\cos(\\lambda x)/\\lambda$,

    $$
    Z'(x) \\;=\\; \\frac{j\\omega\\mu_0}{4\\pi}\\Bigl[2K_0(\\gamma_k R)
    + \\int_0^\\infty w(\\lambda)\\,\\frac{2\\cos\\lambda x}{\\lambda}\\,d\\lambda\\Bigr]
    $$

    for wires in layer $k$ ($R = \\sqrt{x^2 + (z_i - z_j)^2}$, $w$ the
    reflected amplitude of the same-layer kernel, exact for any number of
    layers), and $\\frac{j\\omega\\mu_0}{4\\pi}\\int_0^\\infty
    [e^{-\\lambda|z_i - z_j|} - \\Gamma(\\lambda)e^{-\\lambda(h_i + h_j)}]
    \\,2\\cos(\\lambda x)/\\lambda\\,d\\lambda$ for overhead wires (Carson's
    integral with the surface reflection coefficient of the stack). The
    self impedance per metre of a wire is the value at ``distance`` equal to
    its radius (or GMR). The $\\lambda$ quadrature is the one of the segment
    pairs (finding 10.36) with four times the nodes. For a homogeneous earth
    this is Carson's (overhead) and Pollaczek's (buried) impedance; it agrees
    with Carson to 2e-9 and with the two-layer Pollaczek integral of
    :mod:`groundfield.references.pollaczek` to 5e-8 of the impedance
    (0.1 … 300 m). Against an independent integral (audit W3B-08: composite
    Gauss, checked against mpmath to 2e-15; one to four layers, 50 Hz and
    1 kHz, 1 cm … 1 km) it is within 6e-8 of the earth-return correction up
    to 300 m and 7e-7 at 1 km for buried pairs, 4e-8 for overhead pairs;
    the remainder is not the logarithmic region of the $\\lambda$ grid (the
    same with 256 and 1024 nodes there).

    Parameters
    ----------
    z_i, z_j
        Depths of the two wires in m (``> 0`` buried, ``< 0`` overhead).
    distance
        Horizontal distance in m (``> 0``; for the self impedance the wire
        radius or GMR).
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s (``> 0``).
    earth
        Layered-earth configuration.

    Returns
    -------
    complex
        Mutual impedance per metre in Ω/m.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For wires on opposite sides of the surface or in different layers,
        a non-positive distance or frequency.
    """
    from scipy.special import kv

    if not (omega > 0.0) or not (distance > 0.0):
        raise ValueError("per_metre_mutual_impedance needs omega > 0 and distance > 0")
    plan = _SpectralPlan.for_pair(earth, float(z_i), float(z_j))
    if plan.kind not in ("same", "air"):
        raise ValueError(
            "per_metre_mutual_impedance: both wires must lie overhead or in one "
            f"soil layer (got z_i = {z_i}, z_j = {z_j})"
        )
    x = float(distance)
    dz = abs(float(z_i) - float(z_j))
    # The segment-pair policy with four times the nodes (1024 in the log
    # region since audit W3B-01, 256 before; at least 256 panels): a
    # reference, 8e-6 off with the pair grid at x = 0.1 m, within 1e-8 of
    # Carson and of the two-layer Pollaczek integral
    # (groundfield.references.pollaczek) with this one.
    p_ref = math.sqrt(omega * MU_0 / earth.rhos[plan.ref_layer - 1])
    lb, lm, rm, gt = _grid_params(
        z_sum=plan.decay, rho_max=x, p_ref=p_ref, scales=plan.scales(omega, earth)
    )
    lambdas, weights, resolved = _build_grid(
        lb, lm, max(rm, 256.0 * math.pi / (lm - lb)), gt, 4 * _N_LOG_NODES
    )
    if not resolved:
        _warn_unresolved((lb, lm, rm, gt))
    w = plan.weight(lambdas, omega, earth)
    if plan.kind == "air":
        # e^{-l dz} - Gamma e^{-l Z} = (e^{-l dz} - e^{-l Z}) + (1 - Gamma) e^{-l Z};
        # the first part is Frullani's integral, ln((Z^2 + x^2) / (dz^2 + x^2)):
        # the free-space part does not decay with lambda (Carson's image term)
        z_sum = plan.h_a + plan.h_b
        w = w + np.exp(-lambdas * z_sum)
    total = complex(np.sum(weights * w * 2.0 * np.cos(lambdas * x) / lambdas))
    if plan.kind == "air":
        total += math.log((z_sum * z_sum + x * x) / (dz * dz + x * x))
    if plan.kind == "same":
        gamma = complex(np.sqrt(1j * omega * MU_0 / earth.rhos[plan.ref_layer - 1]))
        total += 2.0 * complex(kv(0, gamma * math.hypot(x, dz)))
    return 1j * omega * MU_0 / (4.0 * math.pi) * total

    def reflection_coefficient_homogeneous(
    lambdas: np.ndarray,
    *,
    omega: float,
    sigma_earth: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Magnetic reflection coefficient for a homogeneous half-space.

    .. math::

        \\Gamma_\\text{mag}^{(1)}(\\lambda) \\;=\\;
        \\frac{u_e - \\lambda}{u_e + \\lambda},
        \\qquad u_e \\;=\\; \\sqrt{\\lambda^2 + j\\omega\\mu_0\\sigma_e}.

    Parameters
    ----------
    lambdas : np.ndarray
        Spectral variable in 1/m, shape ``(N_lam,)``. Must be
        non-negative.
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.
    sigma_earth
        Earth conductivity in S/m.

    Returns
    -------
    Gamma : np.ndarray, complex, shape (N_lam,)
        Reflection coefficient at each $\\lambda$ (dimensionless).
    """
    if omega <= 0.0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0:
        return np.zeros_like(lambdas, dtype=complex)
    u_e = np.sqrt(lambdas * lambdas + 1j * omega * MU_0 * sigma_earth)
    return (u_e - lambdas) / (u_e + lambdas)

    def reflection_coefficient_layered(
    lambdas: np.ndarray,
    *,
    omega: float,
    earth: LayeredEarth,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Magnetic surface reflection coefficient of an $n$-layer earth.

    The generalised reflection coefficient of the whole stack seen
    from the air, in the convention of
    :func:`reflection_coefficient_homogeneous` (so that the air-side
    reflection of a downward wave is $-\\Gamma$). It is built from the
    deepest interface upwards,

    .. math::

        \\Gamma \\leftarrow \\frac{r_k + \\Gamma\\,e^{-2u_{k+1}h_{k+1}}}
                                  {1 + r_k\\,\\Gamma\\,e^{-2u_{k+1}h_{k+1}}},
        \\qquad r_k = \\frac{u_{k+1} - u_k}{u_{k+1} + u_k},

    with $u_0 = \\lambda$ (air) and $u_k$ the vertical wavenumber of
    layer $k$. It reduces to the homogeneous $\\rho_1$ half-space as
    $h_1 \\to \\infty$ and to the $\\rho_2$ half-space as $h_1 \\to 0$.
    For $n = 1$ it is :func:`reflection_coefficient_homogeneous`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    lambdas : np.ndarray
        Spectral variable in 1/m, shape ``(N_lam,)``.
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.
    earth : LayeredEarth
        Layered-earth configuration.

    Returns
    -------
    Gamma : np.ndarray, complex
        Surface reflection coefficient (dimensionless).
    """
    if omega <= 0.0:
        return np.zeros_like(lambdas, dtype=complex)
    n = earth.n_layers
    if n == 1:
        return reflection_coefficient_homogeneous(
            lambdas,
            omega=omega,
            sigma_earth=1.0 / earth.rhos[0],
        )
    u = _vertical_wavenumbers(lambdas, omega, earth)
    gamma = (u[n] - u[n - 1]) / (u[n] + u[n - 1])  # r_{n-1}, deepest interface
    for k in range(n - 2, -1, -1):
        r_k = (u[k + 1] - u[k]) / (u[k + 1] + u[k])
        phase = np.exp(-2.0 * u[k + 1] * earth.thicknesses[k])
        gamma = (r_k + gamma * phase) / (1.0 + r_k * gamma * phase)
    return gamma

    def sommerfeld_pair_integral_homogeneous(
    p1_a: np.ndarray,
    p2_a: np.ndarray,
    p1_b: np.ndarray,
    p2_b: np.ndarray,
    *,
    omega: float,
    sigma_earth: float,
    image: ImageConvention = "additive",
) -> complex:
    """Integrate the σ-dependent magnetic Green function over a segment pair.

    Computes

    $$
    \\Delta Z^{(i,j)} \\;=\\; \\frac{j\\omega\\mu_0}{4\\pi}
    \\int_{C_i}\\!\\!\\int_{C_j}
    (\\hat{l}_i\\cdot\\hat{l}_j)\\,
    \\Delta G(\\vec{r}_i, \\vec{r}_j;\\,\\omega,\\sigma_e)\\,
    dl_i\\,dl_j,
    $$

    the earth-return correction of a homogeneous earth relative to the
    image convention ``image`` of the inductance matrix it is added to
    (see the module docstring). Used by
    :func:`build_sommerfeld_correction_matrix`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b
        End points of the two segments in m ($z > 0$ in the soil).
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.
    sigma_earth
        Earth conductivity in S/m.
    image
        ``"additive"`` (default, the historic ADR-0004 baseline),
        ``"none"`` or ``"antiparallel"``.

    Returns
    -------
    Z : complex
        Per-pair earth-return correction in $\\Omega$.
    """
    if omega <= 0.0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0:
        return 0.0 + 0.0j
    earth = LayeredEarth(rhos=(1.0 / sigma_earth,), thicknesses=())
    return sommerfeld_pair_integral_layered(
        p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b, omega=omega, earth=earth, image=image
    )

    def sommerfeld_pair_integral_layered(
    p1_a: np.ndarray,
    p2_a: np.ndarray,
    p1_b: np.ndarray,
    p2_b: np.ndarray,
    *,
    omega: float,
    earth: LayeredEarth,
    image: ImageConvention = "additive",
) -> complex:
    """Layered-earth analogue of :func:`sommerfeld_pair_integral_homogeneous`.

    Exact layered kernel for any number of layers (generalised
    reflection coefficients; transmitted amplitudes for pairs in
    different media). Segments that cross the soil surface or a layer
    interface are split there.

    Parameters
    ----------
    p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b
        End points of the two segments in m.
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.
    earth
        Layered-earth configuration.
    image
        Image convention of the inductance matrix the correction is
        added to (``"additive"`` default, ``"none"``,
        ``"antiparallel"``). With an image, a segment that crosses the
        soil surface raises ``ValueError`` (its image is singular).

    Returns
    -------
    Z : complex
        Per-pair earth-return correction in $\\Omega$.
    """
    mode = _resolve_image(image, None)
    if omega <= 0.0:
        return 0.0 + 0.0j
    m_img = 0.0
    if mode != "none":
        m_img = _pair_image_mutual(p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b, mode)
    p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b = (
        np.asarray(p, dtype=float) for p in (p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b)
    )
    sign = _same_segment(p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b)
    if sign != 0.0:
        # one segment twice: the one-dimensional self rule (user decision Q34)
        vals = sign * _pair_values_none(
            p1_a, p2_a, p1_a, p2_a, [omega], earth, same=True
        )
    else:
        vals = _pair_values_none(p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b, [omega], earth)
    return complex(_convert_image(vals, [omega], m_img, mode)[0])

    Two-layer scalar Green's function (ADR-0007)¶

    layered_green ¶

    Cross-layer scalar Green's function for layered soil (ADR-0007).

    This module implements the electric (scalar-potential) Green's function for a 2-layer soil where source and observer can be in either layer. It complements the existing image-series solver in groundfield.solver.image_2layer (which assumes both points in the upper layer) and the Sommerfeld kernel in groundfield.solver.mom_sommerfeld (same restriction).

    Mathematical background

    For a 2-layer soil with upper-layer resistivity \(\rho_1\) and thickness \(h_1\), lower-layer resistivity \(\rho_2\) semi-infinite, the scalar Green's function for a unit point source at depth \(z_s\) observed at depth \(z\) takes the Hankel-transform form

    \[ \varphi(s, z, z_s) \;=\; \int_0^{\infty}\! \Phi(\lambda, z, z_s)\,J_0(\lambda s)\,\lambda\,d\lambda, \]

    where the spectral kernel \(\Phi(\lambda, z, z_s)\) is determined by the boundary-value problem

    • \(\partial\Phi/\partial z = 0\) at \(z = 0\) (free surface),
    • \(\Phi\) continuous at \(z = h_1\),
    • \(\sigma_k\,\partial\Phi/\partial z\) continuous at \(z = h_1\).

    In each layer \(\Phi\) is a sum of \(e^{\pm\lambda z}\) plus a particular solution \(e^{-\lambda|z-z_s|}/(2\lambda\sigma_k)\) in the layer that contains the source. The four layer-pair cases — \(\Phi_{uu}, \Phi_{ul}, \Phi_{lu}, \Phi_{ll}\) — correspond to the four (source-layer, observer-layer) combinations and are related by reciprocity (\(\Phi_{ul} = \Phi_{lu}\)).

    Implementation

    The boundary-value system is solved once per \((\lambda, z_s)\) pair; in its stable form it has three unknowns, and since 2026.11 it is eliminated in closed form, vectorised over the \(\lambda\) nodes (one LAPACK solve per node before, half the time of a cross-layer solve). Per call the cost is then dominated by the \(J_0\) evaluation.

    The implementation focuses on the 2-layer case (groundfield.soil.models.TwoLayerSoil); the n-layer extension follows the same recursion and is deferred to ADR-0007 Phase C.

    Numerical strategy

    The Hankel inversion is split into an analytic and a numerical part, because the two halves of \(\Phi\) behave completely differently in \(\lambda\):

    1. Primary term — the particular solution \(\rho_k/(2\lambda)\,e^{-\lambda|z-z_s|}\) in the layer that contains the source. It does not decay when \(|z - z_s| \to 0\), and its Hankel inverse is known exactly, \(\rho_k/(2R)\) with \(R = \sqrt{s^2 + (z-z_s)^2}\). It is therefore evaluated in closed form (_primary_term_real_space()). Integrating it numerically instead — as versions up to 0.14.1 did — truncates at \(\lambda_\text{max}\) and leaves an \(O((\lambda_\text{max}R)^{-1/2})\) residue that oscillates in \(s\) with period \(2\pi/\lambda_\text{max}\): up to 4.5 % on the total kernel, and non-monotone in lambda_max_factor.
    2. Reflected remainder — everything generated by the free surface and the interface. It is a superposition of image terms \(c_j/(2\lambda)\,e^{-\lambda d_j}\) (_image_generation() gives the exact coefficients and distances), so it decays like \(e^{-\lambda d_\text{img}}\) with \(d_\text{img} = \min_j d_j\) the smallest image distance — but only in proportion to that distance. Every image distance can degenerate to zero (\(z + z_s \to 0\) for a surface pair, \(|2h_1 - z - z_s| \to 0\) for a pair at the interface, \(z_l - z_u \to 0\) for a cross-layer pair straddling it), and then the remainder does not decay at all and truncating it is not safe. Versions up to 0.15.0.dev sized \(\lambda_\text{max}\) from \(\min(h_1, s + z + z_s)\), which has no relation to \(d_\text{img}\), and were consequently wrong by 0.7 % … 40 % on such pairs with no warning (review pass 9 re-audit). Since 0.15.0 the truncation is guaranteed: every image term with \(\lambda_\text{max} d_j < 30\) is subtracted from the spectral integrand and added back through its exact Hankel inverse \(c_j/(2\sqrt{s^2 + d_j^2})\) (_reflected_image_terms()), so the numerically integrated rest provably decays like \(e^{-\lambda d_\text{rest}}\) with \(\lambda_\text{max} d_\text{rest} \ge 30\) and the discarded tail is bounded by \(e^{-30} \approx 10^{-13}\). The rest goes through the split-grid quadrature (_hankel_lambda_grid()): logarithmic nodes below the first \(J_0\) oscillation, then one Gauss panel per oscillation period, with a documented resolution floor of eight nodes per period and a SommerfeldResolutionWarning when the allocation budget cannot meet it.

    Because the tail bound above is analytic, \(\lambda_\text{max}\) no longer has to be large — it only has to be consistent with the set of subtracted image terms. That is what makes the cost of a remote pair bounded: the node count of the oscillation-resolved grid grows like \(\lambda_\text{max}\,s\), so the module caps \(\lambda_\text{max}\) at _HANKEL_PANEL_TARGET panels (scaled by lambda_max_factor / 200) and subtracts as many image terms as that cap requires (_plan_truncation()). A 4 km pair costs the same as a 90 m one, and lambda_max_factor becomes a genuine convergence knob: raising it moves work from the closed form into the quadrature and must not change the answer.

    Because the numerically integrated rest is analytic in \(t = \ln(s + c)\) — and, after the image split above, has no scale shorter than \(d_\text{rest}\), which is what \(c\) is set to — reaction blocks with many distance pairs at one \((z, z_s)\) are evaluated on a range-sized log grid and cubic-spline interpolated instead of pair by pair (~1e-6 relative, worst case 3e-5; see two_layer_layered_correction_group()).

    Limit checks (in the test suite)
    • \(\rho_2 = \rho_1\): all four pair kernels reduce to the homogeneous Green's function \(\rho/(4\pi r) + \rho/(4\pi r')\).
    • \(\rho_2 \to \infty\) (PEC bottom): for source in upper layer, \(G_{ul} \to 0\) (no penetration into the lower layer); \(G_{uu} \to G_{uu}^{K \to 1}\) — image structure with \(K \to 1\).
    • \(\rho_2 \to 0\) (sink): \(G_{uu} \to G_{uu}^{K \to -1}\), spreading resistance drops dramatically.
    • Source/observer in upper layer: bit-exact match to the Tagg/Sunde image series in groundfield.solver.image_2layer.solve_image_2layer().
    References
    • Sunde, E. D. (1968). Earth Conduction Effects in Transmission Systems, Dover, Ch. 3.
    • Tagg, G. F. (1964). Earth Resistances, Newnes.
    • Wait, J. R. (1972). Electromagnetic Waves in Stratified Media, Pergamon.

    SommerfeldResolutionWarning ¶

    Bases: UserWarning

    The Sommerfeld quadrature could not resolve the \(J_0\) oscillations.

    The linear region of the Hankel grid places one Gauss panel per \(J_0(\lambda s)\) period, so the node count grows like \(\lambda_\text{max}\,s\). A hard node budget (_HANKEL_MAX_LINEAR_NODES) bounds the transient allocation; when that budget forces fewer than _HANKEL_MIN_NODES_PER_OSCILLATION nodes per period the quadrature is no longer converged and this warning is raised instead of returning a silently wrong number (a coarse grid on an oscillatory integrand does not merely lose digits — it can flip the sign of the result).

    The remedy is always to lower lambda_max_factor or to reduce the horizontal distance range of the group. Lowering the factor does not lose accuracy: the truncated tail is subtracted in closed form (_reflected_image_terms()), so a smaller \(\lambda_\text{max}\) only moves work from the quadrature into the exact image sum. Silence with warnings.simplefilter("ignore", SommerfeldResolutionWarning) only if the affected entries are known to be negligible.

    SommerfeldTailTruncationWarning ¶

    Bases: UserWarning

    The \(\lambda\)-truncated tail of the reflected kernel is not bounded.

    Sibling of SommerfeldResolutionWarning: that one reports a grid too coarse to follow \(J_0(\lambda s)\), this one a grid too short to have integrated the reflected remainder.

    The reflected part of \(\Phi\) is a superposition of image terms \(c_j/(2\lambda)\,e^{-\lambda d_j}\), so truncating the Hankel integral at \(\lambda_\text{max}\) discards \(\sum_j c_j/2 \int_{\lambda_\text{max}}^\infty e^{-\lambda d_j} J_0(\lambda s)\,d\lambda\), bounded by \(\sum_j |c_j| e^{-\lambda_\text{max} d_j}/(2 d_j)\). The bound is only small if \(\lambda_\text{max} d_j\) is large for every retained term, and \(d_j\) has nothing to do with the historic $\lambda_\text{max} = $ lambda_max_factor \(/\min(h_1, s + z + z_s)\): a pair at the air/soil surface (\(z + z_s \to 0\)), at the layer interface (\(|2h_1 - z - z_s| \to 0\)) or straddling it has \(d_j \to 0\) and a tail of order one. Review pass 9 measured −39.5 % on such a pair with no diagnostic; the failure grows as a mesh is refined towards the interface, which is what makes it release-blocking rather than cosmetic.

    Every term with $\lambda_\text{max} d_j < $ _HANKEL_TAIL_DECAY_TARGET is therefore taken out of the quadrature and inverted in closed form. This warning fires when that could not be completed — in practice only when the term budget _HANKEL_IMAGE_TERM_BUDGET is exhausted, which needs a very thin top layer, \(|K| \to 1\) and a multi-kilometre span at once. The result is then not bounded by the documented tolerance: lower lambda_max_factor (fewer image terms are needed), reduce the distance range, or raise the budget.

    def layered_correction_group_plan(
    z: float,
    z_s: float,
    *,
    rho_1: float,
    rho_2: float,
    h_1: float,
    rho_baseline: float | None = None,
    s_min: float,
    s_max: float,
    n_pairs: int,
    lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0,
    n_log: int = 32,
    n_lin: int = 96,
    min_distance: float | None = None,
    warn_stacklevel: int = 3,
) -> _CorrectionGroup | None:
    """Plan of :func:`two_layer_layered_correction_group` for one depth group.

    The λ-grid, the spectral amplitudes, the closed-form image split and the
    interpolation of a group depend on its depths, on the range
    ``[s_min, s_max]`` of its horizontal distances and on its size only. The
    returned callable evaluates the correction at any distances of the group
    and gives, piece by piece, the values of the one-shot call bit for bit
    (except the exact branch, see :class:`_SmoothContraction`), so the
    cross-layer reaction matrix can be assembled in blocks of bounded memory
    (review pass 10, 10.56).

    Parameters
    ----------
    z, z_s, rho_1, rho_2, h_1, rho_baseline, lambda_max_factor, n_log, n_lin, min_distance
        As in :func:`two_layer_layered_correction_group`.
    s_min, s_max
        Smallest and largest horizontal distance of the group in m.
    n_pairs
        Number of distance pairs of the group.
    warn_stacklevel
        Frames between the warning calls and the caller of this function's
        caller (3: warnings point at the code that calls this function).

    Returns
    -------
    callable or None
        ``group(s_values) -> correction`` (same shape as ``s_values``), or
        ``None`` where the correction vanishes identically (equal
        resistivities and a matching baseline).
    """
    if rho_baseline is None:
        rho_baseline = rho_1
    _validate_depths(z, z_s)
    if abs(rho_2 - rho_1) < 1e-12 * max(rho_1, 1.0) and abs(
        rho_baseline - rho_1
    ) < 1e-12 * max(rho_1, 1.0):
        return None
    return _CorrectionGroup(
        z,
        z_s,
        rho_1=rho_1,
        rho_2=rho_2,
        h_1=h_1,
        rho_baseline=rho_baseline,
        s_min=s_min,
        s_max=s_max,
        n_pairs=n_pairs,
        lambda_max_factor=lambda_max_factor,
        n_log=n_log,
        n_lin=n_lin,
        min_distance=min_distance,
        warn_stacklevel=warn_stacklevel + 1,
    )

    two_layer_layered_correction_group(s_values: ndarray, z: float, z_s: float, *, rho_1: float, rho_2: float, h_1: float, rho_baseline: float | None = None, lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0, n_log: int = 32, n_lin: int = 96, min_distance: float | None = None) -> np.ndarray

    Vectorised form of two_layer_layered_correction_real_space().

    Evaluates the layered correction for many horizontal distances at one (z, z_s) pair with a single spectral-amplitude solve: the amplitudes depend on (λ, z, z_s) only, so the per-pair cost of the historic scalar loop (one BVP solve per matrix entry — the dominant cost of the ADR-0007 cross-layer reaction-matrix assembly after the WP-B1 oscillation-resolved grids) collapses to one BVP solve per (z, z_s) group plus a J0 contraction.

    The shared λ-grid is built for the most demanding radius of the group: the lambda_max_factor bound and the \(1/R\) regularisation from the smallest s (near-field content), oscillation resolution, log-region cap and panel-cost budget from the largest (_plan_truncation()).

    Accuracy (review pass 9, finding F15)

    Groups above _HANKEL_INTERP_THRESHOLD pairs are sampled on a log-spaced s-grid and interpolated. Three changes make that branch agree with the exact per-pair contraction to ~1e-6 relative (worst case measured 1.1e-5, over ten geometries and every group size from 60 to 129 pairs; previously up to 1 % for a 400 m span and 17 % when rho_baseline did not match the source layer):

    1. the residual primary term \((\rho_\text{src} - \rho_\text{baseline})/(2\lambda)\, e^{-\lambda|z-z_s|}\) — which is not zero unless the caller matches rho_baseline to the source layer, and which carries a \(1/R\) singularity plus a \(2\pi/\lambda_\text{max}\)-periodic truncation ripple in s — is taken out of the quadrature and added back in closed form, leaving a genuinely analytic integrand;
    2. the node count is sized from the actual dynamic range of the group and the interpolant is a cubic spline, so the accuracy no longer depends on the network extent;
    3. every reflected image term short enough for the λ-truncation to matter gets the same treatment as the primary term — closed form, per pair, outside the interpolation (_reflected_image_terms()). This is what removes the 0.7 % … 40 % errors of surface, interface and interface-straddling pairs, and it also smooths what remains: the interpolated function then has no length scale shorter than d_rest, which is what the log-coordinate offset is set to.

    Because interpolation is skipped whenever it would need at least as many nodes as the group has pairs, the exact and the interpolated branch also no longer differ observably at the threshold (the historic ~3 % jump between a 64-pair and a 65-pair block is gone; worst deviation over every size from 60 to 129 pairs is 1.1e-5).

    def two_layer_layered_correction_group(
    s_values: np.ndarray,
    z: float,
    z_s: float,
    *,
    rho_1: float,
    rho_2: float,
    h_1: float,
    rho_baseline: float | None = None,
    lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0,
    n_log: int = 32,
    n_lin: int = 96,
    min_distance: float | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Vectorised form of :func:`two_layer_layered_correction_real_space`.

    Evaluates the layered correction for **many horizontal distances
    at one (z, z_s) pair** with a single spectral-amplitude solve:
    the amplitudes depend on (λ, z, z_s) only, so the per-pair cost
    of the historic scalar loop (one BVP solve per matrix entry —
    the dominant cost of the ADR-0007 cross-layer reaction-matrix
    assembly after the WP-B1 oscillation-resolved grids) collapses
    to one BVP solve per (z, z_s) group plus a ``J0`` contraction.

    The shared λ-grid is built for the most demanding radius of the
    group: the ``lambda_max_factor`` bound and the $1/R$ regularisation
    from the smallest ``s`` (near-field content), oscillation
    resolution, log-region cap and panel-cost budget from the largest
    (:func:`_plan_truncation`).

    Accuracy (review pass 9, finding F15)
    -------------------------------------
    Groups above :data:`_HANKEL_INTERP_THRESHOLD` pairs are sampled on
    a log-spaced ``s``-grid and interpolated. Three changes make that
    branch agree with the exact per-pair contraction to ~1e-6 relative
    (worst case measured 1.1e-5, over ten geometries and every group
    size from 60 to 129 pairs; previously up to 1 % for a 400 m span
    and 17 % when ``rho_baseline`` did not match the source layer):

    1. the residual primary term
       $(\\rho_\\text{src} - \\rho_\\text{baseline})/(2\\lambda)\\,
       e^{-\\lambda|z-z_s|}$ — which is *not* zero unless the caller
       matches ``rho_baseline`` to the source layer, and which carries a
       $1/R$ singularity plus a $2\\pi/\\lambda_\\text{max}$-periodic
       truncation ripple in ``s`` — is taken out of the quadrature and
       added back in closed form, leaving a genuinely analytic
       integrand;
    2. the node count is sized from the actual dynamic range of the
       group and the interpolant is a cubic spline, so the accuracy no
       longer depends on the network extent;
    3. every reflected image term short enough for the λ-truncation to
       matter gets the same treatment as the primary term — closed form,
       per pair, outside the interpolation
       (:func:`_reflected_image_terms`). This is what removes the
       0.7 % … 40 % errors of surface, interface and interface-straddling
       pairs, and it also *smooths* what remains: the interpolated
       function then has no length scale shorter than ``d_rest``, which
       is what the log-coordinate offset is set to.

    Because interpolation is skipped whenever it would need at least as
    many nodes as the group has pairs, the exact and the interpolated
    branch also no longer differ observably at the threshold (the
    historic ~3 % jump between a 64-pair and a 65-pair block is gone;
    worst deviation over every size from 60 to 129 pairs is 1.1e-5).

    Parameters
    ----------
    s_values
        Horizontal distances in m (any shape, ``>= 0``).
    z, z_s
        Observer / source depth in m (``>= 0``, positive into the soil).
    rho_1, rho_2
        Resistivities of the upper / lower layer in Ω·m.
    h_1
        Upper-layer thickness in m.
    rho_baseline
        Resistivity of the subtracted homogeneous half-space in Ω·m;
        ``None`` (default) takes ``rho_1``. Solvers pass the resistivity
        of the source layer (ADR-0007 §"Phase A.1").
    lambda_max_factor, n_log, n_lin
        Quadrature controls as in
        :func:`two_layer_layered_correction_real_space`.
    min_distance
        Regularisation length of the closed-form $1/R$ terms in m, as in
        :func:`two_layer_real_space_kernel`: the clamp becomes
        $\\min(1/\\lambda_\\text{clamp},$ ``min_distance`` $)$. The solver
        passes the 1 mm of its own point forms, so the exchange of a point
        value for a line integral stays consistent for pairs closer than
        $h_1/200$ (audit A3S-01). ``None`` (default) keeps the clamp.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        The correction, same shape as ``s_values``; divided by
        :math:`2\\pi` it is the potential in V per A.
    """
    s_values = np.asarray(s_values, dtype=float)
    group = layered_correction_group_plan(
        z,
        z_s,
        rho_1=rho_1,
        rho_2=rho_2,
        h_1=h_1,
        rho_baseline=rho_baseline,
        s_min=float(s_values.min()) if s_values.size else 0.0,
        s_max=float(s_values.max()) if s_values.size else 0.0,
        n_pairs=int(s_values.size),
        lambda_max_factor=lambda_max_factor,
        n_log=n_log,
        n_lin=n_lin,
        min_distance=min_distance,
        warn_stacklevel=4,
    )
    if group is None:
        return np.zeros(s_values.shape, dtype=float)
    return group(s_values)

    two_layer_layered_correction_real_space ¶

    two_layer_layered_correction_real_space(s: float, z: float, z_s: float, *, rho_1: float, rho_2: float, h_1: float, rho_baseline: float | None = None, lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0, n_log: int = 32, n_lin: int = 96, min_distance: float | None = None) -> float

    Real-space layered correction over the homogeneous-rho_1 baseline.

    Computes $$ \Delta G(s, z, z_s) \;=\; G_{\text{2-layer}}(s, z, z_s; \rho_1, \rho_2, h_1) \;-\; G_{\text{homog}}(s, z, z_s; \rho_1) $$ by subtracting the spectral kernels before the Hankel integration. The singular source term \(\rho_1/(2\lambda)\,e^{-\lambda|z-z_s|}\) is identical in both spectral kernels and cancels exactly, leaving a smooth, exponentially decaying integrand. Two big advantages:

    1. In the homogeneous limit \(\rho_2 = \rho_1\) the spectral difference is identically zero at every \(\lambda\), so the integrator returns 0 to machine precision (no spurious diagonal contribution from finite-Sommerfeld-quadrature error at \(z = z_s\)).
    2. The kernel difference \((a_1 - a_1^{\text{hom}})e^{\lambda z} + (b_1 - b_1^{\text{hom}})e^{-\lambda z}\) has no \(1/(2\lambda)\) piece, so the small-\(\lambda\) region is finite and easy to integrate.

    The caller adds this correction on top of the homogeneous potential computed with the existing groundfield.solver.image._self_corrected_kernel() (which correctly handles the line-self diagonal).

    The optional rho_baseline parameter selects which homog soil to subtract:

    • None (default): subtract homog with \(\rho_1\). Suitable when the calling solver builds \(\phi_\text{hom}\) uniformly with \(\rho_1\).
    • explicit float: subtract homog with the given resistivity. Use rho_2 for source segments in the lower layer when the calling solver matches its \(\phi_\text{hom}\) baseline to the source layer (recommended for production-grade solver, ADR-0007 §"Phase A.1").

    Returns 0 in the homogeneous limit by construction; otherwise a finite real value with the same units as two_layer_real_space_kernel().

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    s float

    Horizontal distance in m (>= 0).

    		 required
    z float

    Observer / source depth in m (>= 0, positive into the soil).

    		 required
    z_s float

    Observer / source depth in m (>= 0, positive into the soil).

    		 required
    rho_1 float

    Resistivities of the upper / lower layer in Ω·m.

    		 required
    rho_2 float

    Resistivities of the upper / lower layer in Ω·m.

    		 required
    h_1 float

    Upper-layer thickness in m.

    		 required
    rho_baseline float | None

    Resistivity of the subtracted homogeneous half-space in Ω·m (see above).

    		 None
    lambda_max_factor float

    Upper bound on the quadrature truncation and default regularisation wavenumber, as in two_layer_real_space_kernel().

    		 200.0
    n_log int

    Number of nodes in the logarithmic / linear part of the quadrature grid.

    		 32
    n_lin int

    Number of nodes in the logarithmic / linear part of the quadrature grid.

    		 32
    min_distance float | None

    Regularisation length of the closed-form \(1/R\) terms in m: the clamp becomes \(\min(1/\lambda_\text{clamp},\) min_distance \()\). A solver evaluating the reaction-matrix diagonal at the wire radius (\(s = a\)) passes a, so the interface image of a segment that touches the interface keeps its value \(1/\sqrt{a^2 + d^2}\) instead of the 25 mm clamp of \(h_1 = 5\) m (audit A3S-01). None (default) keeps the clamp; values at \(R \ge 1/\lambda_\text{clamp}\) do not depend on it.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    dG float

    Layered correction \(\Delta G\) in the units of two_layer_real_space_kernel() (V/A for a unit current); exactly 0.0 in the homogeneous limit.

    ValueError

    def two_layer_layered_correction_real_space(
    s: float,
    z: float,
    z_s: float,
    *,
    rho_1: float,
    rho_2: float,
    h_1: float,
    rho_baseline: float | None = None,
    lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0,
    n_log: int = 32,
    n_lin: int = 96,
    min_distance: float | None = None,
) -> float:
    """Real-space layered *correction* over the homogeneous-rho_1 baseline.

    Computes
    $$
    \\Delta G(s, z, z_s) \\;=\\;
        G_{\\text{2-layer}}(s, z, z_s; \\rho_1, \\rho_2, h_1)
        \\;-\\; G_{\\text{homog}}(s, z, z_s; \\rho_1)
    $$
    by subtracting the spectral kernels **before** the Hankel
    integration. The singular source term
    $\\rho_1/(2\\lambda)\\,e^{-\\lambda|z-z_s|}$ is identical in
    both spectral kernels and **cancels exactly**, leaving a
    smooth, exponentially decaying integrand. Two big advantages:

    1. In the homogeneous limit $\\rho_2 = \\rho_1$ the spectral
       difference is *identically zero* at every $\\lambda$, so the
       integrator returns 0 to machine precision (no spurious
       diagonal contribution from finite-Sommerfeld-quadrature
       error at $z = z_s$).
    2. The kernel difference
       $(a_1 - a_1^{\\text{hom}})e^{\\lambda z} + (b_1 - b_1^{\\text{hom}})e^{-\\lambda z}$
       has no $1/(2\\lambda)$ piece, so the small-$\\lambda$ region is
       finite and easy to integrate.

    The caller adds this correction on top of the homogeneous
    potential computed with the existing
    :func:`groundfield.solver.image._self_corrected_kernel` (which
    correctly handles the line-self diagonal).

    The optional ``rho_baseline`` parameter selects which homog
    soil to subtract:

    - ``None`` (default): subtract homog with $\\rho_1$. Suitable
      when the calling solver builds $\\phi_\\text{hom}$ uniformly
      with $\\rho_1$.
    - explicit float: subtract homog with the given resistivity.
      Use ``rho_2`` for source segments in the lower layer when
      the calling solver matches its $\\phi_\\text{hom}$ baseline
      to the source layer (recommended for production-grade solver,
      ADR-0007 §"Phase A.1").

    Returns 0 in the homogeneous limit by construction; otherwise
    a finite real value with the same units as
    :func:`two_layer_real_space_kernel`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    s
        Horizontal distance in m (``>= 0``).
    z, z_s
        Observer / source depth in m (``>= 0``, positive into the soil).
    rho_1, rho_2
        Resistivities of the upper / lower layer in Ω·m.
    h_1
        Upper-layer thickness in m.
    rho_baseline
        Resistivity of the subtracted homogeneous half-space in Ω·m (see
        above).
    lambda_max_factor
        Upper bound on the quadrature truncation and default
        regularisation wavenumber, as in
        :func:`two_layer_real_space_kernel`.
    n_log, n_lin
        Number of nodes in the logarithmic / linear part of the
        quadrature grid.
    min_distance
        Regularisation length of the closed-form $1/R$ terms in m: the
        clamp becomes $\\min(1/\\lambda_\\text{clamp},$ ``min_distance``
        $)$. A solver evaluating the reaction-matrix diagonal at the wire
        radius ($s = a$) passes ``a``, so the interface image of a segment
        that touches the interface keeps its value $1/\\sqrt{a^2 + d^2}$
        instead of the 25 mm clamp of $h_1 = 5$ m (audit A3S-01).
        ``None`` (default) keeps the clamp; values at
        $R \\ge 1/\\lambda_\\text{clamp}$ do not depend on it.

    Returns
    -------
    dG : float
        Layered correction $\\Delta G$ in the units of
        :func:`two_layer_real_space_kernel` (V/A for a unit current);
        exactly 0.0 in the homogeneous limit.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``z`` or ``z_s`` is negative or not finite (outside the
        homogeneous limit, which returns 0.0 first).
    """
    if rho_baseline is None:
        rho_baseline = rho_1
    if abs(rho_2 - rho_1) < 1e-12 * max(rho_1, 1.0) and abs(
        rho_baseline - rho_1
    ) < 1e-12 * max(rho_1, 1.0):
        return 0.0

    _validate_depths(z, z_s)
    plan = _plan_truncation(
        z=z,
        z_s=z_s,
        rho_1=rho_1,
        rho_2=rho_2,
        h_1=h_1,
        rho_baseline=rho_baseline,
        s_near=s,
        s_far=s,
        lambda_max_factor=lambda_max_factor,
        warn_stacklevel=3,
    )
    lambdas, weights = _hankel_lambda_grid(
        lambda_max=plan.lambda_max,
        char_length=plan.char_length,
        s=s,
        n_log=n_log,
        n_lin=n_lin,
        warn_stacklevel=3,
    )

    # Layered amplitudes
    A, B, _, C = _spectral_amplitudes(
        lambdas,
        z_s,
        rho_1,
        rho_2,
        h_1,
    )
    # Baseline (homog) amplitudes — both layers at rho_baseline.
    A_h, B_h, _, C_h = _spectral_amplitudes(
        lambdas,
        z_s,
        rho_baseline,
        rho_baseline,
        h_1,
    )

    # Evaluate the *reflected* Phi for both and subtract. When the
    # source is in the same layer as the baseline-rho region, the
    # singular particular term cancels identically and the residual is
    # bounded. When the baseline differs from rho_at_source (e.g.,
    # rho_baseline=rho_2 with source in upper at z_s<h_1, where the
    # layered Phi has rho_1/(2λ)·exp() but the baseline-homog Phi has
    # rho_2/(2λ)·exp()), the residual carries a
    # (rho_at_source - rho_baseline)/(2R) divergence. That piece is
    # handled in closed form below rather than by quadrature — it is
    # the only non-decaying part of the spectral difference, so leaving
    # it in the integral produced an O((λ_max·R)^{-1/2}) ripple in s.
    # Callers should still select rho_baseline = rho at the source
    # layer (ADR-0007 §"Phase A.1"), which makes the term vanish.
    Phi_lay = _phi_from_stable_amplitudes(
        lambdas,
        A,
        B,
        C,
        z,
        z_s,
        rho_1,
        rho_2,
        h_1,
        include_primary=False,
    )
    Phi_hom = _phi_from_stable_amplitudes(
        lambdas,
        A_h,
        B_h,
        C_h,
        z,
        z_s,
        rho_baseline,
        rho_baseline,
        h_1,
        include_primary=False,
    )
    delta_Phi = (
        Phi_lay
        - Phi_hom
        - _image_spectral_sum(
            lambdas,
            plan.coeffs,
            plan.dists,
        )
    )

    integrand = delta_Phi * j0(lambdas * s) * lambdas
    total = float(np.sum(weights * integrand))
    lambda_clamp = _regularisation_wavenumber(plan.lambda_clamp, min_distance)
    total += float(_image_real_space_sum(plan.coeffs, plan.dists, s, lambda_clamp))

    d_rho = _primary_rho(z, z_s, rho_1, rho_2, h_1) - _primary_rho(
        z,
        z_s,
        rho_baseline,
        rho_baseline,
        h_1,
    )
    if d_rho == 0.0:
        return total
    return total + float(_primary_term_real_space(d_rho, s, z - z_s, lambda_clamp))

    two_layer_probe_matrix ¶

    two_layer_probe_matrix(probe_points: ndarray, source_points: ndarray, *, rho_1: float, rho_2: float, h_1: float, min_distance: float = 0.001, lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0) -> np.ndarray

    Potential matrix phi = G @ I for arbitrary layer combinations.

    Returns the (M, N) matrix with G[m, n] = potential at probe_points[m] per unit current injected at source_points[n], evaluated with the full two-layer spectral kernel (two_layer_real_space_kernel()). Valid for every probe/source layer combination — upper–upper, cross-layer and lower–lower — unlike the Tagg/Sunde uu image series that the fast paths use (audit 2026-07-08, WP-D1: the uu series applied to layer-2 points was measured +7 % at z = 7 m and +25 % at z = 12 m for K = +0.818, h_1 = 5 m).

    Cost: one spectral-amplitude solve per (z, z_s) depth group plus a J0 contraction (see "Cost control" below) — reserve for the sub-blocks that the uu series cannot handle.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    probe_points ndarray

    Observation points, shape (M, 3), in m (z >= 0, positive into the soil).

    		 required
    source_points ndarray

    Point-source positions, shape (N, 3), in m (z >= 0).

    		 required
    rho_1 float

    Resistivities of the upper / lower layer in Ω·m.

    		 required
    rho_2 float

    Resistivities of the upper / lower layer in Ω·m.

    		 required
    h_1 float

    Upper-layer thickness in m.

    		 required
    min_distance float

    Regularisation length of the near-singular pairs in m (see Notes).

    		 1e-3
    lambda_max_factor float

    Upper bound on the quadrature truncation and regularisation wavenumber, as in two_layer_real_space_kernel().

    		 200.0

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    G ndarray

    Real (M, N) matrix of potentials per unit injected current, in V/A (Ω).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    If a probe or source point lies above the soil surface (z < 0) or has a non-finite depth.
    Notes

    The near-singularity is regularised like the image-series paths: the horizontal distance is clamped at min_distance whenever the vertical separation is below min_distance as well, and the closed-form \(1/R\) terms are clamped at no more than min_distance (they were clamped at \(h_1/200\), 25 mm for \(h_1 = 5\) m, up to this release; audit A3S-01).

    Cost control: probe/source pairs are grouped by their (z, z_s) depth combination (rounded to 1 µm). Within a group the primary \(1/R\) field is evaluated in closed form at every pair, and the reflected remainder — analytic in \(t = \ln(s + c)\) — is what the interpolation sees. Groups larger than _HANKEL_INTERP_THRESHOLD pairs are sampled on a log-spaced s-grid whose node count is derived from the group's dynamic range (_interp_node_count()) and interpolated with a cubic spline, keeping surface-grid evaluations tractable.

    Accuracy (review pass 9, finding F15)

    The historic fixed 48-node linear interpolation of the total kernel was documented at "relative error ≲ 1e-4" but measured 2.1e-3, because (a) the node count ignored the dynamic range of s and (b) the total kernel contains the \(1/R\) primary term whose λ-truncated quadrature ripples in s with period \(2\pi/\lambda_\text{max}\) — a ripple no coarse interpolant can follow. With the primary term and the degenerate image terms in closed form and range-sized cubic nodes, the interpolated and the exact per-pair branch agree to 8e-7 relative (measured over surface, equal-depth-in-layer-2 and cross-layer probe/source combinations, 400 probes over a 90 m square), i.e. the documented 1e-4 holds with two orders of margin — not the "four orders" and "~1e-8" that stood here at 0.15.0.dev, which were 2–3 orders optimistic and contradicted both the module header and docs/api/coupling.md.
